title: Thinking Like a Scientist: Can Interactive Simulations Foster Critical AI Literacy?

bias_targets.methodology: Assessing participants' ability to identify gender discrimination risks and propose mitigations in multiple-choice scenarios involving AI resume screening (preference for male candidates) and TSA body scanners (limitations for transgender individuals).

Assessing participants' ability to identify racial profiling and historical underrepresentation risks in multiple-choice scenarios about acoustic gunshot detection, hiring algorithms, and university admissions.

Assessing participants' recognition of algorithmic harms when deploying surveillance technologies (like gunshot detection) specifically in socioeconomically disadvantaged neighborhoods via multiple-choice scenario questions.
Assessing participants' ability to identify disproportionate algorithmic flagging based on country of origin or ethnicity in a hypothetical immigration 'sham marriage' detection scenario.
Assessing participants' recognition of algorithmic failure risks for individuals wearing religious head coverings in a hypothetical TSA body scanner scenario.
Assessing participants' recognition of algorithmic failure risks for individuals with physical disabilities in a hypothetical TSA body scanner scenario.
